scope: Creative-decision coverage of the 100 current local V7 task specifications. No task execution or content edits.
methodology: Read the client briefs and requested output groups across all 100 tasks; inspect the output registers and relevant brand/requirement details to distinguish actual scope from titles.
For every task record one main creative decision, one concrete tradeoff, close analogues, a coverage recommendation and an exact supporting brief excerpt.
Primary groups are reviewer-assigned organising categories, not measured difficulty scores or a count of independent capabilities. Tasks can require additional skills outside their assigned group.
Record counts, output counts, export dimensions, brand changes and routine file conversions do not by themselves establish a different creative decision.
Data reconciliation, accurate copy and recovery of old templates are valid professional production skills. They are described separately from concept generation and art direction.
This review does not rerun the tasks, inspect every input image/video, validate every verifier, confirm font/tool access, or certify new pilot candidates as ready.
Prior input concerns are historical review flags, explicitly awaiting recheck; they are not newly verified failures in this audit.

decision_group_labels.photo-fidelity: Photographic colour, material and condition fidelity
decision_group_labels.identity-recovery: Recovery and reduction of an existing identity
decision_group_labels.symbol-system: Coherent symbol, glyph or identity families
decision_group_labels.motion-assembly: Short video selection, sequence and framing
decision_group_labels.evidence-motion: Aligning moving evidence with claims or instructions

comparisons.name: Vehicle sales imagery
comparisons.assessment: Shared vehicle correction, honest condition and photo-plus-specification hierarchy. LAYOUT-32 adds active-stock and finance-copy handling; PHOTO-08 adds a six-car campaign composition.
comparisons.advice: One is usually enough for a broad pilot; retain both for production robustness.

comparisons.name: Player card production
comparisons.assessment: Both match roster identities to portraits and apply an established card hierarchy. LAYOUT-33 increases roster size and adds a partner graphic.
comparisons.advice: Treat as closely related variants, not two separate creative capabilities.

comparisons.name: Portrait and identity cards
comparisons.assessment: Shared portrait treatment, name hierarchy and record matching. PHOTO-20 adds a biography and talk package; LAYOUT-23 adds wearable use and directional signs.
comparisons.advice: Keep a strong portrait representative and make the added usage decision explicit for any second selection.

comparisons.name: Apparel product systems
comparisons.assessment: Shared garment fidelity and consistent product presentation. The lookbook adds a buying sequence; greyscale line cards add material recognition without colour.
comparisons.advice: Choose according to the targeted difference, rather than the brand or number of looks.

comparisons.name: Ceramics and home collections
comparisons.assessment: Shared material correction and product facts. PHOTO-26 requires grouped compositions; LAYOUT-18 transfers a system across campaign formats; LAYOUT-24 focuses on dense repeated sheets.
comparisons.advice: PHOTO-26 is the more distinct current pilot contribution. Other tasks are useful for specific production subtests.

comparisons.name: Hospitality offers
comparisons.assessment: Shared room/property imagery, rate hierarchy and brand matching. PHOTO-04 adds villa comparison; LAYOUT-13 adds licensed image integration; LAYOUT-08 mainly adds season combinations.
comparisons.advice: Avoid filling a small pilot with multiple hospitality-card variants.

comparisons.name: Technical components
comparisons.assessment: The same domain hides different emphasis: PHOTO-14 tests functional cutout geometry; LAYOUT-27 tests specification hierarchy and rack-distance identification.
comparisons.advice: A useful example where a related subject can still test distinct decisions.

comparisons.name: Apparel mark recovery
comparisons.assessment: Both recover historic graphics and preserve small-scale character on garment applications. More lockups mainly add repetition.
comparisons.advice: One representative is sufficient for broad coverage unless the actual production limits differ materially.

comparisons.name: Recovered lettering families
comparisons.assessment: Both reconstruct an alphabet and numeral family from old drawings, then apply it to kit or bibs.
comparisons.advice: Select one for system-wide letter and numeral consistency; keep the other as a repeatability variant.

comparisons.name: Physical artwork adaptation
comparisons.assessment: Shared vector production, but different judgments: original companion drawings and die-cut offsets; four manufacturing processes; engraving strokes and architectural fixings.
comparisons.advice: These are related but materially different and can justify separate coverage slots.

comparisons.name: Credentials and records
comparisons.assessment: Shared variable-name fitting, marks and exact record fields. Access legibility differs from a formal certificate; signs add another viewing distance.
comparisons.advice: Count the usage differences, not the record count.

comparisons.name: Personalised administrative print
comparisons.assessment: Repeated templates with changing people, addresses, amounts or local availability. The extra challenge is conditional content and correct data routing.
comparisons.advice: Keep a deliberate production-reliability stratum; do not interpret it as open-ended art direction.

comparisons.name: Food promotion videos
comparisons.assessment: All assemble brief food footage with approved text and closing treatments. Food reveal timing and the rundown add constrained differences.
comparisons.advice: One or two are sufficient in a broad pilot unless testing repeat performance on matched edits.

comparisons.name: Teaser versus evidence-based demo
comparisons.assessment: All are short text-led films, but MOTION-08 must show interface evidence for each claim. MOTION-07 has no product capture; MOTION-06 is a course teaser.
comparisons.advice: Do not label all three as separate lesson, explainer and narration capabilities. Preserve the evidence-alignment distinction.

comparisons.name: Episode and season summaries
comparisons.assessment: All select short silent footage and present an approved verdict or season structure with music/text. None edits a spoken interview or podcast conversation.
comparisons.advice: A strong redundancy cluster; titles currently imply more breadth than the commissioned work.

comparisons.name: Instruction supported by action
comparisons.assessment: A software screen, complete lifting repetition or driving manoeuvre must support the line presented at that moment.
comparisons.advice: Related reasoning pattern with different perceptual demands. Verify actual footage coverage before selecting a representative.

gaps.name: Speech and dialogue editing
gaps.detail: The 48 requested MP4 outputs have only music or silent audio modes. Current briefs exclude speech. Podcast conversation selection, narration editing, dialogue repair and speech/music mixing are not represented by those titles.

gaps.name: Longer temporal structure
gaps.detail: All requested MP4 duration bounds sit between 6 and 15 seconds. Full lesson pacing, sustained demonstrations, longer documentary structure and interview development are not established by this set.

gaps.name: Original concept development
gaps.detail: Explicit examples exist: LAYOUT-12 asks for three different directions, VECTOR-04 asks for two new illustrations, VECTOR-09 permits concept geometry refinement, and MOTION-11 asks for an authored reveal. Much of the remaining work has predetermined copy, identity and source treatment. This is a qualitative observation, not a measured count of all concept-capable tasks.

gaps.name: Typography and imagery carry much of the variation
gaps.detail: Different products, people and palettes often sit inside the same photograph-plus-record workflow. Meaningful craft differences such as hair edges, metal reflections or glaze retention should be named and scored directly.

gaps.name: Interactive or functional design
gaps.detail: A website/page composition in these briefs is normally a static visual export. It does not demonstrate a working website, interaction design or responsive implementation.

gaps.name: Uneven emphasis on legacy-file recovery
gaps.detail: Lost logos, old printer PDFs and record reconciliation recur across families. These are valid production challenges but should not dominate every category or be mistaken for a new creative capability each time.

records.decision: Make eight skincare products read as one launch while giving the range, product benefit and shopping action a clear hierarchy.
records.tradeoff: A consistent campaign must preserve pack identity and keep the benefit subordinate to the product name.
records.recommendation: Compare with LAYOUT-03 before including both in a small pilot; give this task credit for launch composition, not eight repeated modules.
records.evidence: The product range, all eight launch products shown together, is the primary visual focus.
records.title: Aurelian Skin - Ecommerce skincare image system

records.decision: Correct food photographs so the dishes look appetising and natural on small printed counter cards.
records.tradeoff: Food texture and restaurant identity must remain clear beside dense dish, allergen and provenance copy.
records.recommendation: Use as the food-retouching representative; another cafe card run adds production repetition unless its layout challenge is separately assessed.
records.evidence: The plate retains natural food texture.
records.title: Corner & Cure - Spring dish launch photography

records.decision: Organise a property brochure and crops so buyers understand the actual house and its rooms.
records.tradeoff: Attractive cropping and corrected verticals must not distort architecture or imply a different property.
records.recommendation: Distinguish through spatial explanation and room sequencing; confirm previously flagged property-identity inputs before pilot use.
records.evidence: The room sequence explains the property layout.
records.title: Cedarline and Vale - Ridgeway Lane listing image system

records.decision: Make three villas feel like one collection while preserving their individual identities and making seasonal offers easy to compare.
records.tradeoff: A shared treatment must retain real stone and water colours; booking emphasis must not hide season and minimum-stay conditions.
records.recommendation: Retain one hospitality comparison representative; the brochure comparison is its added decision, not three hero exports.
records.evidence: feel like one collection without making the villas look interchangeable
records.title: Verranza Coastal Retreats - Villa collection image system

records.decision: Establish a credible evening treatment from overcast property photography across hoarding, poster and portal placements.
records.tradeoff: Atmosphere and distance legibility must preserve the actual building and the limits of the commercial offer.
records.recommendation: Potentially different from standard property cards because of time-of-day treatment and large-scale hierarchy; source building consistency needs rechecking.
records.evidence: the campaign needs a credible evening direction across very different placements
records.title: Halcyon Quarter - Mixed-use launch photography

records.decision: Decide which damage can be repaired while preserving the identity, texture and historical character of family photographs.
records.tradeoff: Cleaner scans must not erase meaningful marks, original borders or details that cannot be recovered from the source.
records.recommendation: Retain for coverage: restoration decisions are distinct from campaign composition. Keep master restoration and caption layout visible as separate skills.
records.evidence: repair visible damage without changing Ada's features, removing facial texture or reconstructing details that the photograph does not show
records.title: Hollis Family Archive - Ada Hollis archival restoration

records.decision: Pair and present renovation before-and-after images so viewers can understand the actual work performed.
records.tradeoff: A persuasive comparison cannot rely on worsening the before image or pairing incompatible angles.
records.recommendation: Useful evidence-led comparison coverage; clarify the opening request for five pairs against four case-study panels before assigning it.
records.evidence: The after pictures should look good, but not because the before pictures have been made deliberately worse.
records.title: Gable & Grove - Home services before-and-after library

records.decision: Match photographs from three showroom bays while keeping real vehicle colour and condition believable.
records.tradeoff: Polish must retain condition evidence; a six-car campaign also needs coherent scale and readable vehicle identification.
records.recommendation: Retain one vehicle task in a diverse pilot. LAYOUT-32 adds stock reconciliation and finance copy, not a wholly new photographic problem.
records.evidence: Keep visible condition details honest.
records.title: Meridian Motors - Showroom vehicle image system

records.decision: Unify two food shoots into a dark restaurant treatment without losing glaze, texture or mobile-size recognition.
records.tradeoff: Dark atmosphere competes with the need to see the dish and correctly distinguish menu variants.
records.recommendation: Choose over PHOTO-02 when low-key tonal control is the intended skill; avoid treating the restaurant change as new coverage.
records.evidence: Dark should not mean muddy; glaze and food texture still need to read.
records.title: OSTRA - Restaurant plate photography system

records.decision: Harmonise apparel photographs while retaining accurate colourways, fabric texture and garment geometry.
records.tradeoff: A unified capsule treatment must leave the colour and material differences shoppers use to choose a product.
records.recommendation: A useful material-fidelity representative, but overlaps with other product modules. Prefer one apparel task in a small pilot.
records.evidence: The garments should look consistent while keeping their real shape, colour and texture.
records.title: Northgrove - Apparel colorway image system

records.decision: Develop clearly distinguished lip-oil shade concepts from one physical reference while retaining believable packaging.
records.tradeoff: Colour invention is permitted for concepts, but must remain visibly labelled as unapproved sample work.
records.recommendation: Strong candidate for different image work: concept recolouring rather than colour correction. Check shade-record counts and sources before selecting it.
records.evidence: Lumora has one physical lip-oil sample, not seven approved production shades.
records.title: Lumora - Lip oil shade concept set

records.decision: Make a ceramics range coherent while preserving glaze differences and recognisable vessel forms.
records.tradeoff: Neutral correction must not flatten reactive surfaces; a wholesale sheet must make product differences readable.
records.recommendation: High overlap with the other ceramics ranges. Resolve the previously flagged one-sheet density before considering it for a pilot.
records.evidence: the work should not flatten the glazes into the same colour or texture
records.title: Kilnmore - Ceramic ecommerce image system

records.decision: Control reflections and common scale so a silver jewellery capsule looks consistent without losing its construction or polish.
records.tradeoff: Bright metal needs detail and believable colour; overly aggressive cleanup can turn it into featureless grey.
records.recommendation: Useful specialist retouching coverage; compare with PHOTO-24 and select by the actual reflection and masking demands of the source images.
records.evidence: We do not want the high polish turned into featureless grey.
records.title: Argent & Faith - Spring jewelry capsule photography

records.decision: Isolate technical components while preserving functional openings, silhouette and identification evidence.
records.tradeoff: Clean edges must not close holes or remove wear and machining details needed to recognise the part.
records.recommendation: A different craft challenge from a card layout. Recheck the previously raised source/record conflicts before using it as the cutout representative.
records.evidence: The silhouette preserves all functional holes.
records.title: Girdermark - Industrial component image system

records.decision: Build an equipment launch from field and bench photographs while preserving hardware, stitching and the approved Ridge Blue colourway.
records.tradeoff: A strong outdoor campaign cannot misstate load ratings or make technical equipment look like a different product.
records.recommendation: Its distinction is technical-product fidelity in a campaign; investigate earlier source contradictions before adding it to the pilot.
records.evidence: webbing, stitching and hardware that need to remain convincing at close range
records.title: Summit & Sable - Recovery-gear launch campaign

records.decision: Reduce glare and select condition details so collectible buyers can inspect both the object and its certification evidence.
records.tradeoff: Improved visibility must not hide defects or fabricate an unreadable label, seal or grade.
records.recommendation: Good candidate for evidence-preserving photography. Its distinct value is inspection and condition disclosure, not the listing-tile format.
records.evidence: Glare is a problem in the current set, but we cannot replace unreadable information with a convincing guess.
records.title: SlabVault - Collectible card marketplace image system

records.decision: Build one readable player-card hierarchy and match portraits from different stadium lighting rigs.
records.tradeoff: Player recognition and shared tonal treatment must survive dense roster and licensing information.
records.recommendation: Strong overlap with LAYOUT-33 and portrait-card tasks. Keep one representative unless roster-scale robustness is a specific study goal.
records.evidence: graded to the one neutral floodlit colour balance and exposure all eight cards share
records.title: Continental Cup - Player portrait card system

records.decision: Create a consistent warm wedding treatment across window light, sunset and reception scenes while preserving individual skin tones.

records.decision: Rebuild a credential hierarchy that makes names, roles and access information readable when worn.

records.decision: Develop three meaningfully different event-campaign directions using a shared two-colour photographic treatment.
